\begin{example} \end{example}[Cayley complex of $\Z _n$] ↗ def:cayley-graph-and-complex ↗ ex:real-projective-space-covering 1. ch1:1.47\group Covering Spaces

For $G=\langle x\mid x^n\rangle =\Z _n$, the quotient is $S^1$ with a disk attached by degree $n$, while the Cayley complex is $n$ disks sharing their boundary circle. For $n=2$ this is $S^2\to \RP ^2$. \end{example}
